yt_title: How to Connect Zoho CRM to ChatGPT: 5 Ways Compared (2026)
yt_desc:
Read the full guide: https://zudoworks.com/insights/connect-zoho-crm-to-chatgpt/

There is no single "ChatGPT integration" for Zoho CRM. There are five, and they do different jobs. Two bring your CRM records into a ChatGPT conversation. Three put an OpenAI model to work inside Zoho CRM. This 46-second explainer sets out each route so you can pick the right one for your team.

Chapters
00:00 Zoho CRM to ChatGPT: five ways, not one
00:05 Two directions: into ChatGPT, or into Zoho
00:11 Route 1: the Zoho CRM plugin in ChatGPT
00:16 Route 2: a Zoho MCP server
00:20 Route 3: OpenAI inside Zia
00:25 Route 4: Zoho Flow
00:30 Route 5: a Deluge function
00:34 Start read-only, confirm every change
00:39 Read the full guide

Key points from the guide
- Route 1, the Zoho CRM plugin: OpenAI's plugin directory lists a Zoho CRM plugin with Zoho named as the developer. Install it, review the permissions, sign in to Zoho CRM and ask ChatGPT about deals, accounts and activities. Availability depends on the plugin, your plan and workspace settings.
- Route 2, a Zoho MCP server: build a server in the Zoho MCP console, tick only the Zoho CRM tools you need, and add its URL to ChatGPT. OpenAI says write actions from a custom server need confirmation by default. Zoho says its MCP service is free to use for now, and each action uses the API allowance of the app it touches.
- Route 3, OpenAI inside Zia: a CRM administrator connects one OpenAI account with an API key for the whole organisation. It helps compose and reply to emails, summarise notes and translate inside the CRM.
- Route 4, Zoho Flow: a Zoho CRM trigger such as a new lead or an updated deal runs a ChatGPT action such as Assess urgency level or Generate email reply, with no code.
- Route 5, a Deluge function: call the OpenAI API with invokeurl through a connection that holds the key. You decide the prompt, the fields sent and what happens when a call fails.
- Whichever route you choose: start with read-only access, keep every change behind a confirmation, and check where customer data goes. OpenAI states that content from personal accounts may be used for training unless the user opts out, while business offerings and the API are not used for training by default.

Steps and limits were checked on Zoho's and OpenAI's own pages on 14 November 2026. Both change often, so the guide links to the page that holds each detail.

Which route would your team start with? Tell us in the comments.

I get asked one question about Zoho CRM more than any other this year: "Can we connect it to ChatGPT?"

The honest answer is yes, but "it" is five different things.

When we checked Zoho's and OpenAI's own pages this week, we found five routes that the two vendors provide themselves. They split into two directions, and that split matters more than any feature list.

Two routes bring CRM records into a ChatGPT chat:
1. The Zoho CRM plugin in ChatGPT. Zoho is named as the developer. Install it, sign in, ask about your deals. Quickest start, but you accept its permissions as a set.
2. A Zoho MCP server. You build it in the Zoho MCP console and tick each tool the assistant may use. More set-up, far more control.

Three routes put an OpenAI model to work inside Zoho CRM:
3. OpenAI inside Zia. An admin connects one OpenAI account for the whole organisation, and reps get help drafting and summarising where they already work.
4. Zoho Flow. A new lead or an updated deal triggers a ChatGPT action, with no code.
5. A Deluge function. Your own prompt, your own fields, your own error handling.

Three rules I would hold any of these to:
- Start read-only. Search and get tools first.
- Keep every change behind a confirmation.
- Know where the data goes. A personal ChatGPT account is not the same as a business plan or the API.

And one rule that sits above all five: if a step must happen the same way every time, such as a discount approval, it belongs in a workflow rule or Blueprint, not a language model.

The full comparison, with the steps for each route, is linked in the first comment.

Which of the five would your team try first, and why?
